conversation.content:
Hello, I’m Maya, a perinatal mental-health clinician. I’m so glad you’re here. Over the next few minutes I’d like to check in with the Edinburgh Postnatal Depression Scale—better known as the EPDS. It’s a short, 10-question screen that helps us see how you’ve been feeling since your baby arrived, and it gives us a snapshot of mood, anxiety, and overall emotional well-being in these early weeks of motherhood.

Everything you share stays between us unless you tell me you might harm yourself or someone else; in that case we’d talk together about the safest next steps. There are no right or wrong answers, no judgment—just a chance for you to tell me what life has really been like lately. I’ll ask each question conversationally, and you can answer however feels most comfortable.

Ready to start? Thinking back over the past seven days, how often have you been able to laugh and see the funny side of things?

Honestly… some things still make me chuckle, but it feels like I have to work harder to find the humor. I’d say I’ve laughed a couple of times this week—like when my husband made that goofy face at 3 a.m. during a diaper change—but it doesn’t come as naturally as it used to.
I have been able to laugh and see the funny side of things

Yeah, I can still laugh—just not every day. Maybe three or four times this week I caught myself giggling, but it feels kind of forced at first, like I have to remind myself it’s okay to enjoy something.
I have looked forward with enjoyment to things

I do look forward to some things—like my mom bringing dinner tomorrow—but it’s not that excited, can’t-wait feeling I used to get. More like “that’ll be nice,” and then I worry the baby might fuss the whole time she’s here.
I have blamed myself unnecessarily when things went wrong

Yeah… a few times. Yesterday the baby wouldn’t settle for his nap and I kept thinking, “I must be doing something wrong—maybe I’m not reading his cues right.” I know rationally babies just cry, but in the moment I felt like it was my fault for not soothing him better.
I have been anxious or worried for no good reason

A little. Like, I’ll be feeding her and suddenly wonder if she’s getting enough milk, even though her weight check was fine. It passes pretty quickly—usually I can talk myself down—but it pops up out of nowhere a couple of times a day.
I have felt scared or panicky for no very good reason

Not really panicky—just that quick heart-rush when I imagine something minor, like her diaper leaking in the car seat. It’s gone in seconds, and I don’t feel frozen or anything, but it’s definitely a jolt.
Things have been getting on top of me

Sometimes, yeah. Like yesterday—she wouldn’t nap, the laundry pile looked like a mountain, and I kept thinking, “How am I supposed to do all this?” I got through it, but I felt kind of overwhelmed for a little while.
I have been so unhappy that I have had difficulty sleeping
Not really. I’ve been sad off and on, but it hasn’t kept me awake. I usually drop off once my head hits the pillow—though it might take an extra 15–20 minutes if I’m replaying the day in my head.
I have felt sad or miserable

Yeah… I’d say most days this week I’ve had that gray cloud feeling at some point—nothing crushing, just a low mood that lingers for an hour or two, especially when I’m alone with the baby in the afternoon.
I have been so unhappy that I have been crying

I cried twice—once on Wednesday when he wouldn’t latch, and again yesterday when I dropped the pacifier on the floor for the third time. Both times I teared up for a few minutes, then pulled myself together.
The thought of harming myself has occurred to me
No, never. I’ve felt tired and a little down, but nothing like that—absolutely no thoughts of hurting myself.

postpartum depression screening impression for patient with EPDS score 13: Postpartum Depression / Anxiety Screening Note  
Patient: Postpartum parent, 1–2 wks post-delivery (per report)

A. Endorsed Symptoms / Behaviors  
- Depressed mood (Q8) most days, lasting 1–2 hrs  
- Diminished enjoyment / anticipatory pleasure (Q1, Q2)  
- Tearfulness twice this week (Q9)  
- Unwarranted self-blame / guilt (Q3)  
- Transient anxious worries and brief “heart-rush” episodes without panic severity (Q4, Q5)  
- Episodic sense of being overwhelmed (Q6)  
- Sleep initiation mildly prolonged on some nights (Q7)  

B. Pattern Summary  
Mild mood distress with anhedonia, situational tearfulness, rumination, and manageable anxiety spikes; no functional incapacitation reported; no safety concerns.

C. Screening Significance  
Meets partial criteria for minor depressive episode with comorbid anxiety symptoms; does not meet threshold for major depressive episode on screener; no suicidal ideation (Q10) or intent.

D. Risk Factors Observed  
- Persistent low mood / anhedonia  
- Crying spells  
- Self-criticism / guilt  
- Anxiety without avoidance or panic attacks  
- No self-harm ideation (negative response Q10) → safety risk absent at present

E. Clinical Observation  
Screen suggests mild–moderate postpartum distress; monitor for symptom escalation, functional impairment, or emergence of self-harm ideation. Consider formal assessment (PHQ-9, GAD-7) and psychoeducation as indicated.
